Brooklyn-based trio Gooseberry, formed in 2019, melds alternative rock, indie, and blues to craft their distinctive sound. Comprising Asa Daniels (guitar, vocals), Evin Rossington (drums), and Will Hammond (bass), the band has racked up millions of streams and has garnered praise from editorial stalwarts Galore, Under the Radar, and more. They’ve become integral to NYC’s music scene, headlining venues like Bowery Ballroom, as well as supporting notable touring acts such as Ringo Starr, BabyJake, and Tanner Usrey. In September 2024, Gooseberry released their debut full-length album, All My Friends Are Cattle. The album was tracked over the course of three months, predominantly at Precision Sound Studios in New York City. Drums were recorded by Grammy-winner James ‘Jimmy T’ Meslin (Dream Theater, John Petrucci, Rush). Grammy-winning engineer Colin Bryson (Zach Bryan, J Balvin, Willow Avalon) served as producer and recording engineer (reprising his role from the Validate Me EP). Grammy-winner Phil Joly (The Strokes, Lana Del Rey, Daft Punk) mixed the record, and Jennica Best (Colatura) mastered it. The record has already been streamed 3M+ times and counting. Now boasting 70K+ monthly listeners and major festival appearances under their belt, Gooseberry recently officially launched a new chapter with their sophomore LP, Simple Sucker, arriving September 25, 2026. Uncover Music presents Rusty Shackle Rusty Shackle are a hard-gigging folk-rock band from South Wales, known for their infectious energy, anthemic songs, and genre-blurring sound drawn from folk, rock, and indie roots. Since forming in 2010, they've built a loyal following through relentless touring and a reputation for exhilarating live shows that get crowds on their feet. The band have released five studio albums to date, each one expanding their sonic palette while staying rooted in rich melodies, heartfelt lyrics, and a love of storytelling. Their 2022 release, Under a Bloodshot Moon, reached number 2 in the UK Folk Albums Chart and was praised as 'a winner' by Get Ready to Rock and 'their finest album yet' by Liverpool Sound and Vision. Rusty Shackle were awarded Wales' Folk Favourites at the 2023 Wales Folk Awards - a reflection of the powerful connection they've built with audiences across the UK and beyond. Their shows have been described as 'full of hope and optimism... a joy to listen to' (Morning Star), while Folk and Honey celebrated their 'high-energy performances and well-crafted catchy tunes that swim around your head for days.' Whether playing festival stages, packed-out venues, or intimate sessions, Rusty Shackle deliver music that's rousing and resonant - songs that speak from the heart and stay with you long after the final note.

Buoyed by social media savvy, a clever sense of humour and fire hooks, Slayyyter made her way to Los Angeles. In a short spell, the mild-mannered Midwest-born pixie managed to transform into an erotic electronic pop femme fatale. Now, it sounds like she’s stalking the Hollywood Hills with a combination of razor-sharp song-craft, inventive underground production and cheeky lyrics, all while dripping in eighties-inspired afterparty-ready fashion wild enough to make Sharon Stone blush. events.description: The Exploited ARE punk rock ! The first wave of British punk was a bust. In Edinburgh ex-Squaddie Wattie Buchan and his mates were seriously pissed off. Angry at what they saw happening around them – a country in disarray with greedy politicians treating the people like shit; and with Johnny Rotten’s prediction of “No Future” become truer by the day, there was only one way forward – embrace the music that had given you so much and give it something back… your entire life! Thus were spawned THE EXPLOITED.1980 saw the The Exploited launch their first vinyl assault upon stupidity, complacency and corruption when they demolished the indie charts with the one-two knockout of the “Army Life” and “Barmy Army” eps on their own Exploited Records label. Their debut album “Punks Not Dead” launched a new breed of politically outspoken anarcho-punk bands, and become the number one independent album of 1981 – selling 150,000 copies and reaching number 20 in the national charts. A year later ‘Troops Of Tomorrow’ was released and is now recognized as one of the all-time classic punk albums.Anyone unsure of what The Exploited stand for need only read the label on the tin: the band’s albums include ‘Death Before Dishonour’, ‘Beat The Bastards’ and ‘Fuck The System’; and over the decades The Exploited have remained steadfastly true to their roots – never selling out, and never bowing down.

ai.en: Skids and Theatre of Hate play a co-headline tour at The Castle and Falcon in Birmingham.

events.description: Two era defining artists SKIDS & THEATRE OF HATE come together this autumn for an explosive UK co-headline tour.SKIDSThe Skids formed in 1977 in their hometown of Dunfermline, Scotland by Richard Jobson, Stuart Adamson, Bill Simpson & Tom Kellichan. After releasing an independent single the band were played by John Peel, supported The Clash in concert and then were signed to Virgin Records in 1978. Their first singles were "Sweet Surburbia", "The Saints are Coming" and "Into the Valley" - the latter reaching the UK Top Ten in early 1979.The current Skids line up see's the lineup stripped back to an explosive 4 piece with Richard Jobson, Peter Byrchmore (Membranes), Hernandez (Drums) & Connor Whyte (Guitar).THEATRE OF HATEIn 1980, Kirk Brandon formed THEATRE OF HATE from the ashes of heralded punk band The Pack. Joining Kirk on vocals were notable punk musicians Stan Stammers and Luke Rendall, along with old school friend, Steve Guthrie and Canadian born John "Boy" Lennard, who revolutionised the band's sound with his haunting sax lines.Theatre Of Hate's debut double-A-side single, "Legion"/"Original Sin", topped the independent chart in 1980, and "Westworld", their debut album, produced by Mick Jones from The Clash and released in 1982. The single taken from the album, "Do You Believe In The West- world?" has become an anthem and is still widely played in clubs and on international radio, as well as featuring on numerous compilation albums.

events.description: DAY FEVER HAS TAKEN OVER THE COUNTRY! Day Fever prides itself on creating a safe-space where people can just be themselves. No dress code, no egos, just enjoyment and positivity. events.description: Uncover Music presents Ae Mak Inspired mainly by her own spirit, and Bjork, Aldous Harding, Judee Sill, Paul Simon and with the limbs of a young David Byrne; Irish artist Ae Mak (Aoife McCann) has been creating what her friends describe as "nursery rhymes for adults", producing genre-defying other-worldly pop music with industrial beats and charging them into visceral - kinetic stage shows. Her songwriting led her to signing a worldwide publishing deal with BDI Music UK in 2019. Having released a plethora of self-produced EPs, done the Berlin and done the L.A thing, and made a couple of cartoon albums; She has just released her debut record "Folk Songs For Mama & Papa" A cosmical, spiritual - folk work. events.description: AGMP Presents BRUCE FOXTON '50 years of The Jam' Tour + very special guests The Jam released their debut single 'In The City' in 1977 on Polydor Records. Over the next five years The Jam became one of the most important groups that the UK has ever produced with #1 singles such as 'Start!', 'Going Underground', 'Town Called Malice' and 'Beat Surrender'. Bruce Foxton was the bass guitarist on every recording The Jam ever made. He was also lead vocalist and songwriter on songs such as 'News of the World' (which is the theme tune to BBC's 'Mock The Week' TV show), 'Smithers-Jones', 'Carnaby Street' and more. In 2027, Bruce Foxton will be celebrating 50 years of The Jam along with his band Mark Brzezicki (Big Country), Andrew Fairclough (Secret Affair) and Craig Joiner (Romeo's Daughter) along with very special guests. An AGMP Concerts presentation.

ai.en: Caoilfhionn Rose plays The Victoria in Birmingham, presented by Uncover Music. The singer was raised in Manchester.

events.description: Uncover Music presents Caoilfhionn Rose Raised in Manchester, Caoilfhionn developed a "deep, almost spiritual appreciation" of music in all its diversity from a young age. Drawing inspiration from nature, dreams, and personal experiences, she crafts songs that are both intimate and universal in their themes. Inspired to begin writing and performing as well as studying music, Caoilfhionn started playing open mic nights around Manchester around 2013, while simultaneously embarking on a collaboration with The Durutti Column, one of Factory Records' most distinctive and prolific artists- an experience which, she says, "really helped open my mind and music world". A performance at a local café caught the attention of Gondwana Records founder Matthew Halsall, who invited Caoilfhionn to work on her debut album 2018's Awaken. It became the first of three albums for the label; followed by 2021's Truly and 2024's Constellation. As a bandleader she headlined tours across the UK and Europe and has also supported artists such as Mammal Hands, The Breath, GoGo Penguin, Alabaster dePlume and Hania Rani.

events.description: Uncover Music presents Funke and the Two Tone Baby Funke and the Two Tone Baby is a truly unique artiste. 'Greebling' is the process of adding detail to increase the appearance of complexity and this new iteration of Funke promises to be more detailed and more complex than ever before. With the new album featuring guest appearances from Beans on Toast and Samantics, and once again produced by Dutty Moonshine Big Band's production genius, 'Binge', Funke's 5th LP stands head and shoulders above anything he has done so far on his long and dedicated music career. events.description: Uncover Music presents Rowena Wise Rowena Wise is a Naarm/Melbourne-based singer-songwriter whose work balances beauty and mess with rare emotional precision, drawing from 60s folk storytelling while grounded in indie rock, garage pop and alt-folk. Raised in Margaret River, Western Australia, by a luthier father and a Chicago-born folk musician mother, Wise moved to Melbourne at 18 to forge her own path. Since debuting in 2018, she has amassed over 10 million streams, earned airplay across triple j, double j and Unearthed, and toured extensively across Australia, the UK, Europe, the USA and Canada, supporting artists including Holy Holy, Ball Park Music, Bernard Fanning and Paul Dempsey. Her 2024 debut album, Senseless Acts of Beauty, was praised by CLASH Magazine as "carefully etched indie folk" and shortlisted for the Australian Music Prize. Her highly anticipated sophomore album, Bad Things Feel Good*, a tender, point-blank meditation on transformation produced by Rob Muinos (Julia Jacklin, Didirri), is out August 7, 2026 via Beloved.

events.description: AGMP Presents Martin Stephenson & The Daintees hail from the North East of England. Their debut single 'Roll On Summertime' was released in 1982 on Kitchenware Records (home of Prefab Sprout, The Kane Gang, Hurrah!). 'Boat To Bolivia' was the debut album by Martin Stephenson & The Daintees. After appearances on Channel 4's 'The Tube' and BBC2's 'Whistle Test' the album went on to become one of the essential releases of 1986. In 1988, the second Martin Stephenson & The Daintees album 'Gladsome, Humour & Blue' was released which featured the singles 'There Comes A Time' & 'Wholly Humble Heart'. Don't miss Martin Stephenson & The Daintees perform music from the 'Gladsome, Humour & Blue' LP along with other classics and fan favourites. An AGMP Concerts presentation.

ai.en: RUTS DC present 50 years of The Ruts, celebrating their music from 1977 to 2027, at The Crossing with special guests.

events.description: RUTS DC present 50 years of RUTS Music (1977-2027) THE RUTS + special guests In 1977, The Ruts emerged from London with a sound unlike anybody else around them - the raw urgency of punk colliding with reggae, dub and rock, driven by formidable musicianship and a fierce sense of purpose. With Malcolm Owen, Paul Fox, Dave Ruffy and Segs Jennings, The Ruts created a body of music whose power has endured far beyond its original moment. After losing Malcolm Owen in 1980, the remaining members chose integrity over nostalgia by re-inventing themselves as Ruts DC, eventually losing Paul Fox in 2007. Ruts DC remain a living, evolving band to this day. But the time has come to celebrate the whole story. This tour is about taking the music that exploded out of a movement and bringing it onto a stage in 2027 with all its urgency and relevance intact. Music made across five decades - from the albums The Crack and Grin & Bear It, through Animal Now, Rhythm Collision, Music Must Destroy, and Counterculture? with the classic singles In A Rut. Babylon's Burning. Something That I Said. Jah War. Staring At The Rude Boys. West One (Shine On Me) and more. An AGMP Concerts presentation.
